text.text: Your home care agency in one place. Start with Referrals to answer today, then Shifts for the day's visits, and keep Credentials current so every caregiver is always cleared to work. Operational tracking only; care plans and clinical records stay in your clinical system.

text.text: Referrals from hospitals often need care to start within 24 to 48 hours. The agency that answers fast, assesses well and starts on time becomes the agency discharge planners call first.
Add the referral with a short description, source, care needed and
date (today or tomorrow for hospital discharges).
Call the referral source back to confirm you can take the case, and ask: discharge date, diagnosis that affects care, mobility, cognitive status, who is at home, and the funding.

Emergency contacts, physician, pharmacy and medication list recorded
and fill in authorized hours a week, bill rate and the first supervisory visit date (often 30 days after start, then every 60 to 90 days).
Match a caregiver by skills, schedule, distance and personality. Introduce them at the first shift if you can.

Eleanor's discharge planner called at 9 am: hip replacement, home on Friday, needs help bathing and dressing five mornings a week, long-term care policy. The supervisor assessed on Thursday, the policy claim forms went out the same day, and Ottis started Friday at 8.
A good schedule gives clients the same familiar caregivers, keeps caregivers' hours steady, and never leaves a client without a visit.
Every Thursday for the next week
Start from last week's shifts. Keep the same caregiver at the same times wherever you can; continuity matters more than anything to clients with memory loss.
Add each shift with start time, hours and
with authorized hours for each client and fix any gap.
Check each caregiver's total hours and travel. Avoid overtime unless it is planned and approved.
Send each caregiver their schedule and each family the visit times.
Credentials current for every caregiver on the schedule (see Credential tracking).
Skills match the tasks: transfers, hoists, dementia care.
Client preferences honored: gender of caregiver, language, pets, smoking.

text.text: Never let a client find out by no one arriving. A missed shift is marked
No client below authorized hours without a reason
No caregiver above 40 hours without approval
Every shift has care tasks listed
Back-up caregiver named for every client

Build holiday schedules two weeks early and confirm them with families. On snow or storm days, call every client in the morning, keep the visits for people who live alone or need help with medication first, and record any shift that could not happen.

Rosalind's caregiver Casper works her Monday, Wednesday and Friday mornings. When he was out last week, the back-up who had shadowed him twice took the shift, and Rosalind's husband was called the night before.
Every shift is billed and paid from the verified record. Payers that use electronic visit verification will not pay for a visit without a matching clock-in and clock-out at the client's home.
The caregiver clocks in on arrival at the client's home. The shift moves to
The caregiver completes the care tasks and notes anything unusual: a fall, a change in eating, confusion, a skin problem.
The caregiver clocks out before leaving.
Every shift that should have started has a clock-in; late ones get a call within 15 minutes
ticked when clock-in, clock-out and location match the schedule
Mismatches fixed with a written reason (forgot to clock out, phone had no signal) signed by the caregiver
Anything unusual a caregiver reports is passed to the supervisor the same day and to the family by the supervisor. Falls are always reported, even with no injury.

A caregiver with an expired CPR card, TB screen or background check should not be on the schedule. Tracking credentials is how the agency keeps clients safe and passes inspections.
What to track for each caregiver
CPR and first aid (usually every two years)
Criminal background check and registry checks (at hire and as your state requires)
Nursing licence for nurses and aides who need one
Driver's licence and car insurance for caregivers who drive clients
for expiry in the next 60 days.
Tell each caregiver in writing what is due and by when, and book the class or screening if the agency provides it.
When the new card or result arrives, enter the new expiry date and press
. Keep a copy in the personnel file.
A caregiver with an expired credential is taken off the schedule until it is renewed. No exceptions.

Inspectors ask for proof that every caregiver who worked in the last year had current credentials on each shift date. Keeping expiry dates here and copies in the file answers that question in minutes.
One person owns credentials. They hold the list, send the reminders and say no when an expired caregiver is put on the schedule. Back them up when they do; the agency's licence depends on it.
Casper's CPR card expired ten days ago. He was moved off this week's shifts, booked into Saturday's class, and the back-up covered Rosalind's mornings until his new card came in.

The office of a home care agency: new referrals, the clients you serve, the shifts caregivers work, whether each visit was verified, and the credentials that let each caregiver work. Care notes and medical records stay in your care management system.
